scope: Proposition 7.1 of the manuscript “Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs” (preprints/Minimal-models-and-Mori-fibre-spaces-for-generalized-log-canonical-Q-pairs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 036 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 37e6d650c989c3fb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a spread of the algebraic data, retaining the given weights and cutoffs, such that, for all sufficiently large reductions of characteristic p, there is a single product H of regular eigenfunctions with σ = mH = pϕgs + O(1). The error depends on the fixed characteristic-zero data but not on p. For this H and every vector of nonnegative integers (jν), there are a regular nonzero eigenfunction R and integers 0 ≤ ki < p with pmR = σ + ∑ ν jνmtν + k − (p − 1)e, (7.1) pχR = χH + ∑ ν jνχtν + χfk − (p − 1)χη. (7.2) Characters are written additively. For every preassigned cutoff T, any collection of these reduced regular eigenfunctions with distinct pairs (value, character) and weights at most s(worig)T has size at most the characteristic-zero number H(T) of Lemma 6.1.
